author: marcfeuermann
body:
Hi Val, this is not an easy task. In most fungal papers, the mevalonate pathway is considered as the first module of the ergosterol pathway. I agree that is not exclusively involved in ergosterol biosynthesis but I included it in ergosterol pathway in all annotations I've made so far (UniProt, GO, GO-CAM, PAN-GO). It would be an enormous amount of work to change something that is at best questionable...
Below is one example out of many that describe the ergosterol pathway.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20b31f50-ee37-4545-a7ac-35ea01958df9)

author: ValWood
body:
A bit of history, this ticket is based on a decision made on a GO editorial call with @pgaudet  and @thomaspd  and others. I checked multiple times to be sure we wanted to proceed in this was for GO-CAM annotation., I double checked if I should report these mappings.

One issue is that it will lead to inconsistent annotations/representations.
If we include the isoprenoid biosynthesis part of the pathway for ergosterol, why not the same for ubiquinone, dolichol, heme, etc.? We only think of this as ergosterol biosynthesis because they are named ergX and because they were originally isolated as ergosterol-compromised mutants. 
The decision on the call was to begin the ergosterol pathway from the first committed step for ergosterol biosynthesis and connect the ergosterol pathway (and the other downstream pathways) to the isoprenoid pathway/mevalonate module.

This seems to be the general solution we have converged upon for pathway branch points.

I'll raise this again on the next editorial call to see if we do want to do this. Will update.

author: marcfeuermann
body: Just to add my two cents: I think that at the GO-CAM level, it's not a problem to separate these pathways because they can be linked. It's more complex for PAINT-style annotations because the information is completely lost. One solution would be to be a little more complete in the definitions and/or the hierarchy. For example by allowing sub-pathways being part_of several general pathways.
